deck.topic: What surprises Texas transplants (SA, Austin, DFW)
deck.hook: Most transplants misjudge Texas by exactly 47 minutes

points.title: The 47 Minutes
body: On a map, twelve miles looks like nothing.
In Austin or DFW at 5pm, that same twelve miles runs 47 minutes each way. Almost eight hours a week gone.
People pick the house before they drive the route once.
points.loop: That is not the expensive part.

points.title: The Tax Flip
body: No state income tax gets everyone excited on the flight in.
Then the property tax bill lands and the math looks very different depending on which side of a county line you bought on.
points.loop: Your bills are not done yet.

points.title: August Is A Season
body: It is not one hot month. It is a stretch where the ground pulls away from the slab and your electric use doubles.
Locals water the foundation. Newcomers do not know that is a thing.

points.title: Schools By Street
body: Two houses on the same road can feed two different schools.
Boundaries also get redrawn, and growth in San Antonio and north of DFW means they get redrawn often.
points.loop: Then there is the fun problem.

points.title: The Weekend Problem
body: The coast, the Hill Country, and the good barbecue are all within a few hours, and the line starts before you wake up.
Where you live decides how many of those you actually do instead of talk about.
points.loop: Most transplants learn this year three.

linkedinCaption:
Most relocation regret in Texas does not come from the house. It comes from things that never show up on a listing.

Twelve miles on a map can run 47 minutes each way at 5pm in Austin or DFW. No state income tax feels great until the property tax bill arrives and you learn how much a county line matters. August is not a hot month, it is a season, and locals water their foundations for a reason. Two houses on the same street can feed different schools, and those boundaries move as growth pushes north of DFW and around San Antonio.

For those of you who have relocated clients here, which of these catches people off guard most often?
